correctness.rationale: For every integer \(m\ge1\), the two canonical embeddings force at most \(2m\) occurrences of either symbol and exactly \(2m\) of one symbol; otherwise shared zero and one would require contradictory order. Splitting at the middle two zeros forces exterior one-counts \(a=b=j<m\) and central count \(m-j\) by single-deletion minimality. Conversely each such word loses an input subsequence after any deletion. Choosing j ones independently in each anchored arm gives \(\binom{m+j-1}{j}^2\), with a disjoint complemented branch. A direct ratio bound and Stirling establish the geometric deficit limit and total asymptotic. The bundled checker independently exhausts all input words for \(m\le4\) and all proof-eligible words for \(m=5\), with exact agreement; these tests are not substituted for the infinite proof.

value.rationale: Opposite equal binary blocks are a canonical antagonistic two-string merge family. Minimal common supersequences are an emerging object with nontrivial length diversity. The result derives the complete length distribution of irreducible merges, an explicit bijection to independently interleaved arms and a nondegenerate geometric concentration law. These facts are useful as exact analytic benchmarks and identify genuinely different behavior at each feasible length; the motivation is not an arbitrary finite parameter slice.
